To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

multiple scattering and induced radiation modify quark fragmentation functions, that this softening effect depends on both the diagonal and off-diological twist-four parton distribution, and that the modification is quadratically proportional to the nuclear size (A2/3).

the modified quark distribution and fragmentation functions in a nuclear target are obtained by solving the QCD evolution equations, and that they depend on both diagonal (quark-gluon-quark) and off-diagonal (quark-quark-gluon) twist-four parton distribution functions.
multiple scattering leads to modified quark fragmentation and that induced radiation gives rise to a LPM interference pattern that softens the modified fragmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the multiple scattering of the initial-state parton shower, which is a new source of the nuclear modification of parton distributions and fragmentation functions in eA collisions.
a systematic treatment of multiple parton rescattering and its effects on the quark fragmentation functions and the QCD evolution equations.
the study of parton propagation in a dense medium, such as a nucleus or quark-gluon plasma, using the formalism of multiple parton scatterings and the QCD evolution equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multiple scattering in the nuclear medium is an important physical effect and should be considered in the study of deeply inelastic e-A collisions.
the modified fragmentation functions are the most promising probes for the study of multiple parton interactions and the LPM effect in eA scattering.
the modified quark distribution functions are the only ones that can be reliably calculated in QCD, while the modified fragmentation functions are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the multiple-scattering-induced radiation gives a significant contribution to the modification of quark fragmentation functions, which is comparable to or even larger than the contribution from the energy loss of the quark in the medium.

the multiple parton scattering effects on the nuclear modification of fragmentation functions are significant, and the induced radiation is important for the next-leading-twisted parton distributions and fragmentation functions.
the modified fragmentation functions are the key to understand the nuclear modification of hadron spectra in deeply inelastic scattering and the LPM effect plays a crucial role in this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to the well-known modification of the parton distribution in a nucleus, the multiple scattering of partons in the nucleus leads to a modification of the partonic fragmentation functions in deeply-inelastic scattering.
the modified quark distributions in the nuclear medium are not universal and depend on the initial state and the final state observables.
the multiple scattering effects in the medium are more important than the induced radiation effects, and therefore the multiple scattering effects are the leading effects.
